rows.title: I Vitelloni 1953, directed by Federico Fellini | Film review
rows.comment: and governed by an inextricable mixture of affectionate sympathy and acid satire
rows.verdict_le10: and governed by an inextricable mixture of affectionate sympathy and acid satire
rows.dek_lead: Beautifully shot and performed, and governed by an inextricable mixture of affectionate sympathy and acid satire, it clearly (and beneficially) trails the neo-realist roots which Fellini later shook off.

rows.title: CRITIC'S CHOICE/Film; Adrift in Postwar Italy, Perilously Close to 30
rows.comment: lyrical story of a group of young men drifting aimlessly toward 30
rows.verdict_le10: lyrical story of a group of young men drifting aimlessly toward 30
rows.dek_lead: Without Fellini's sweet, lyrical story of a group of young men drifting aimlessly toward 30, we would probably not have ''American Graffiti'' or ''Mean Streets'' or ''Diner.''
